### Addendum, 2026-08-20 late: PR #28's review rounds, and the merge to `main`

The entry above stops at `423ad57`. Seven further commits landed on the branch afterwards, all of them review findings fixed and folded, and none of them was recorded above. They are recorded here.

**The API contract and CI (`830270b`, `d4ad69d`).** Two findings from the gap review. The three `audio.node` problem-type URIs the validation path returns were not declared in `api/openapi.yaml`'s `Problem.type` enum, so the contract did not name errors the implementation could produce; the enum now declares them and a test reads the enum out of the document and fails if the code's set ever grows past it, rather than asserting three fixed strings. And **CI had never built anything with cgo**, so the integration test's own doc comment claiming it exercised "the real cgo backend" rested on the runner's ambient `CGO_ENABLED` default rather than on anything the workflow stated. The test job now has an explicit cgo build step, and the integration harness forces `CGO_ENABLED=1` for the agent and `=0` for the coordinator and `showmeshctl` instead of inheriting the environment unchanged. Three mediums came with them: the two audio-configuration push paths now fan out on detached per-node bounded contexts, so one stuck node no longer poisons the rest and a client disconnect no longer truncates the fan-out; `showmeshctl audio node set` uses `fs.Visit` so `--ltc-channel=0` is distinguishable from the flag being absent and reaches the coordinator's own `400` instead of a local refusal; and the binding's older-revision-refused and same-revision-replay paths gained direct tests, which nothing exercised before.

**The session lifecycle (`66cfc39`, `bbeb7dc`).** `Start` on a still-paused session for the same item reused the pause-time bookmark and could seek the engine backwards; it is now refused. The automatic post-announcement `Resume` got the recoverable-not-`Failed` treatment the operator path already had. `RestoreAll` now releases a redundant in-memory session's engine handle and resets LTC ownership before rebuilding, so two restores in a row cannot leak a handle or strand ownership. Operator-supplied audio settings are validated field by field, with the substituted field named rather than the whole payload accepted or silently replaced. LTC ownership is released on an engine-spontaneous stop, and a fade stranded by natural playlist completion is resolved. Four tests were tightened to prove what their names claimed.

**The engine internals (`f8bbae3`, `f610b11`).** Six findings, each with a test confirmed to fail against the unfixed code. The LTC feeder no longer treats an unresolved `gst.ClockTimeNone` running time as a zero PTS anchor and never reports `LTCRunning` until a genuine running time has been read; **a blocking `GetState` wait was tried first and reverted**, because it stalled the feeder goroutine long enough to starve `interleave`'s LTC sink pad and drag program audio down with it, which the `-race` suite's own program-rate tests caught. `Close` records its reason as its literal first action so `markBroken`'s first-write-wins guard beats a bus error that teardown itself causes. `branchForSource` no longer holds the engine lock across an unbounded `GetParent()` cgo walk. `Resume`'s two-clock read happens back to back, which narrows the sampling gap rather than eliminating it. The LTC feeder goroutine recovers from a panic instead of taking the agent process down. Two test names were corrected to state what they prove, and the encode/decode round trip was mutation-tested by disabling the drop-frame-bit fix and confirming the test catches it. **Several of these are backed by AST guard tests rather than live races**, because the underlying properties could not be reproduced against `fakesink` on this machine; that is stated rather than dressed up as a timing proof.

**One doc-comment correction (`9a1e029`).** `SetSettings` claimed its fallback "is never silent" and pointed at `SettingsValidationIssues` as the observable half. Nothing in production reads that accessor and no coordinator surface reports it, so the comment described a surface that does not exist. Both comments now say the substitution is visible on the node and nowhere else. Giving it an operator-visible surface remains owed, alongside the LTC ownership refusal recorded above with the same defect.

**Merge state.** `origin/main` was merged into the branch at `2ff62be`; the only conflict was `docs/decisions/README.md`, where ADR-042 (this branch) and ADR-043 (`main`, show-scoped Cues) were issued into the same register row and both are kept.

### Addendum, 2026-08-21: the first CI run of this project's cgo, and what it found

**`main` carried no `go-gst` at all.** The dependency is absent from `main`'s `go.mod`, so this branch is the first in this project's history to put cgo, GStreamer and libltc through CI. Nothing before it could have caught any of the following, and every engine measurement recorded above was taken on macOS.

**The agent does not build on the CI runner.** `ubuntu-latest` is Ubuntu 24.04 and ships GStreamer 1.24.2; `go-gst` v0.0.2 calls symbols added in 1.26 (`GstIdStr` and the static-string caps API). Only two `go-gst` versions exist, so there is no downgrade path. **The floor this branch had added to CI asserted GLib 2.80, which 24.04 satisfies**, so the guard passed and the build then failed as a wall of undefined C symbols in a dependency. A version floor that names the wrong library is worse than none: it reports the platform as adequate and moves the failure somewhere unrecognisable.

`test`, `lint` and `vuln` now run in a `debian:trixie` job container, the platform the engine was measured green on, and each asserts `gstreamer-1.0 >= 1.26` alongside the existing GLib floor. **`lint` and `vuln` had never had the GStreamer dev headers at all**, so neither could load the engine packages once they existed; neither had ever linted or scanned them.

**`integration` cannot be a container job.** `scripts/test-integration.sh` starts the real pinned Mosquitto itself, deliberately, so the suite tests the shipped `deploy/mosquitto` config rather than a `services:` stand-in. That needs the host Docker socket and host networking, and GitHub's `container:` field cannot express `--network`. It runs the suite in a nested `golang:1.25.0-trixie` container instead, with the workspace mounted at its own absolute path and `TMPDIR` inside it, so the seed-file bind mounts the script hands to the host daemon resolve identically on both sides.

**Two smaller ones, both container-shaped.** The workspace is checked out by the host runner and read as root inside the container, so git refuses it as dubiously owned and every `-buildvcs` stamp fails as a typecheck error, which is how `lint` reported it. And Debian's `docker.io` only *recommends* `docker-cli`, so `--no-install-recommends` left the integration container with no `docker` binary.

**The FPP integration workflow compiles the whole `test/integration` package**, which reaches the cgo engine even though that suite starts no agent and proves nothing about audio. It now compiles without cgo and states that it does not cover the cgo backend.

**A finished-work gap the merge found.** The review fix that declared the three `audio.node` problem-type URIs in `api/openapi.yaml` never regenerated `ui/src/api/generated/schema.d.ts`, so `make check` failed on `ui-gen-check`. The generated file is checked in and the gate compares against git, so an uncommitted regeneration still reads as stale.

**Two defects the first green-building CI run then found in the engine itself**, both tracked and neither yet closed at the time of writing: a branch joining a running pipeline reporting a position matching the engine's uptime rather than its own start position, deterministic across two runs of the same commit; and `Load: context deadline exceeded` at the full 30 s bound, landing on a different set of tests each run. **Neither reproduces on Linux locally** in a `debian:trixie` container at any of isolation, full package, `-race`, one, two or four CPUs, or amd64 under emulation. The unreproduced condition is the command the `test` job actually runs, `go test -race ./...` across roughly forty packages on a four-core runner, where this package competes with `internal/coordinator/api`'s 570 to 613 second race suite.

**The lesson, and it is this project's recurring one in a new disguise.** A test environment that differs from the deployment environment reports success on exactly that difference, and here the difference was that the deployment environment had never been tested at all: the audio node runs on Linux, every number recorded for it was macOS, and the first Linux run disagreed. The guard that should have caught the platform gap checked the wrong library and waved it through.
## 2026-08-18 (Track F seams F0 through F4, plus F7 CLI coverage for F1: built on `track-f/night-session`, not merged)

**Goal:** build Track F's night-session controller past its specification: F0's FPP evidence capture, F1's configuration kind, F2's persisted lifecycle controller, F3's FPP timeline/playlist integration, F4's cue runner, and the `showmeshctl` coverage F7 requires for what F1 ships. Against fakes, a throwaway bench `fppd`, and F0's recorded observations. No integrated acceptance is claimed and nothing in this session ran against the deployed fleet.

**Completed**, all in the worktree at `/Users/erbartos/Documents/code/showmesh-track-f`, branch `track-f/night-session`:

- **F0, FPP night-loop evidence capture (`369ad34`).** Captured against a dedicated bench `fppd` 9.5.3 on `:8091`, never the shared bench container and never the deployed fleet, with every claim in its `SUMMARY.md` backed by the raw request/response saved beside it. **The finding that reshapes the track: stock FPP has no brightness command at all**, verified against all 40 registered commands in `Commands.cpp` and independently against Step 8's own vocabulary capture. The only brightness-shaped control is a static per-channel-range output processor whose `POST` handler overwrites the entire config file, and `/api/fppd/status` carries no brightness field, so neither half of RESTING-MODE section 7.3's compositional model (observe the ceiling, apply an independent multiplier) is available. F4 therefore implements no brightness fade and readiness rejects a configuration that needs one; the owner decision was queued and answered (see Questions raised, below). Four other measurements shape F3: duration is `FrameCount * StepTimeMS` and nothing else carries it; a playlist definition is readable while idle and distinguishes a bare-FSEQ playlist from one carrying audio; `stopgracefully` returns `Stopping` in about 22 ms while the item plays to its natural end, so completion is the status transition to idle and nothing else; and `milliseconds_elapsed` advances in exact 50 ms quanta, which is the resolution a cue deadline needs. The superseded first cadence poll, taken in the window before the host's Docker daemon died, was deleted rather than kept.
- **F1, the `night.session` and `night.session.active` configuration kinds (`e48660f`).** End to end: the kind and its validation, the versioned API, OpenAPI conformance in both directions, and full `showmeshctl` coverage (F7's slice for what F1 ships). No `audio-playlist` kind is minted; ordered background-audio slots live inside `night.session`, pinned against Track C's `pkg/audio` wire vocabulary (stable `itemId`, `resume` as `resume|restart` rather than a bool, and the package's own `repeat`/`itemTransition` spellings) so F5 has nothing to reconcile. Validation refuses a calendar field at any depth (ADR-038 decision 1), a duplicated rest duration, an empty or duplicate-`itemId` audio list, a crossfade without its duration, a positive gain ceiling, dangling asset and action references, duplicate cue names, and negative durations. `siteControl` and `interlocks` are refused with a problem naming RESTING-MODE section 10 and Track F's F6, rather than accepted and ignored.
- **F2, the persisted night-session lifecycle controller (`49189d7`).** Schema v10, the closed state machine from RESTING-MODE section 3, the seven ADR-038 lifecycle commands, the durable cue outbox table F4 fills, the versioned API and its `nightSession.changed` stream event, and full `showmeshctl` coverage. Every row of RESTING-MODE section 4.4's start-night table and section 4.5's request-final-show table is its own named test.
- **F3, FPP timeline and playlist integration (`63f4770`).** Starting the configured resting playlist, deriving the content boundary from the pinned FSEQ's own duration plus observed position, arming and invalidating relative deadlines, launching the show behind the transition barrier, detecting real playlist completion, and the FPP-facing half of readiness. Also adds `fpp.position.elapsed.ms` to both collectors (identifier reserved on `main` beforehand): absent decodes `unsupported` with a reason, and an explicit `null` decodes as collection failed, never a plausible zero. The seam's own pause capture found something F0 had not exercised: FPP's position counters keep advancing in real time while playback is paused, which is why a paused observation invalidates the boundary outright rather than being adjusted for.
- **F4, the transition action runner and its durable cue outbox (`506c6c0`).** The `enterShow` and `enterResting` cue lists from the pinned revision, dispatched through named logical actions, with barriers where the show launch depends on their outcomes and no protocol path in any cue. RESTING-MODE section 7.1.1's commit boundary is the seam: `showCommitted` and the first outward cue's outbox record are written in one transaction before any dispatch, and **both crash sides are exercised structurally through hooks at the true seam points rather than by racing a timing window.** Retryability was read rather than assumed: only FPP is retryable by identity, because `dispatchFPPCommand` resolves an idempotency hit before its pre-dispatch guard and is structurally incapable of re-sending; Resolume and MQTT are conservatively non-retryable. Schema v10 was amended in place (unmerged) to carry the cue phase in the outbox identity.

**Defects found by review after each seam's own gates were already green.** This is the pattern of the session, and it repeats at every seam:

- **F1 (nine found):** a payload that could not be `PUT` back — `crossfadeMs` carried `omitempty` while the validator required the key present and accepted `0`, so a valid write returned a document missing a field the operator never removed, and the ordinary get/edit/set loop failed on its own output; its round-trip test passed either way because it round-tripped through plain `json.Unmarshal` rather than the real decoder. And two published surfaces claimed cue actions must name a `show.action` in the same show while nothing read the action's show and the checking function took a `show` parameter its body never used. That same-show check is now implemented (extended by orchestrator ruling to `timelineAsset` and every background-audio item, since ADR-027 makes a Show a namespace precisely so programming Christmas cannot break Halloween).
- **F2 (thirteen found, two of them this project's own recorded lessons arriving in a new subsystem):** a degraded session refused every command, including `fade-out-night` and `power-down-presentation`, and nothing anywhere could clear the degraded flag — one coordinator restart mid-transition bricked the controller for every subsequent night, recoverable only by hand-editing SQLite, while the problem detail promised an operator recovery that existed on no surface. That is D-3's guard defect again: a refusal for want of ShowMesh's own evidence is strictly worse than the coordinator being switched off, since a `409` is a successful conversation with a healthy coordinator and fires no fallback. The three admission-closing commands are now exempt from the degraded gate. And the read-decide-write sequence ran outside any transaction: concurrent `start-night` and `fade-out-night` left admission open in 18 of 20 runs while the operator was told the fade applied, and concurrent `prepare-site` produced two sessions and two epochs in 20 of 20 runs. The whole sequence now runs inside one transaction against a `_txlock=immediate` DSN with `SetMaxOpenConns(1)`, serializing by construction rather than by timing.
- **F3 (ten found across two review rounds, most proved by probing the real functions rather than by reading them):** an invalidated boundary silently re-armed — the contradiction check ran and wrote its reason, then the next tick recomputed from the same stale anchor and armed the show anyway while the operator surface still rendered the invalidated boundary; combined with the pause finding above, a resume 100 seconds later launched the show immediately. An invalid boundary is now load-bearing and forces a fresh anchor. The show launch could reach `ifBusy=replace` without a positive identification, three ways, the operational one being evidence 44 seconds old still counting as current against a general 45-second currency window while two missed polls let FPP's own scheduler start something else; replacement now requires the same instance, a non-empty configured name, current playlist evidence, and a five-second age bound rather than the general currency window. And a stale or absent playlist-name signal left an empty string indistinguishable from FPP's genuine idle empty string, read as the show having finished — the ports-payload `ma` defect again, at the point that decides the show is over; observations now carry their own currency flags and missing evidence is `unknown`.
- **F4 (sixteen found across two rounds, several proved by execution):** every cue offset collapsed to zero, because cues ran only after entering `transition-to-show` and that state is entered at the content boundary, so a fade authored twenty seconds before the resting sequence ends ran at the end instead. The audience would have seen the sequence finish at full brightness and everything fade afterwards, which is backwards from section 7.1's staging and defeats two acceptance criteria by name; it also put the commit at the wrong moment, since the first outward cue is normally the earliest fade and therefore precedes the boundary. The show-launch barrier was **unbounded**, so a cue whose adapter never reported completion held the show all night, inverting ADR-035, ADR-031 decision 2 and ADR-029 decision 4 at once: a monitoring gap must never stop a show, and this stopped the show precisely because ShowMesh could not watch. The Track C session's own finding that night, that a single-media audio session never reported completion at all, is the concrete case, and it reached this track from another one while the seam was being built. An adapter error that provably never reached the wire was recorded as `dispatched`, timed out to `ambiguous`, and deadlocked the night with no show, no fade-out (the commit had already made the show final) and only `end-session` as an exit, with an unconfigured Resolume enough to trigger it. An MQTT first cue passed readiness as confirmable while its dispatcher is a stub, committing a show for which nothing was ever emitted. A cue name shared between `enterShow` and `enterResting` resolved the wrong list's row and reported success for a cue that never ran. Five more: a `pending` barrier cue blocked forever despite `onFailure: continue`; the boundary fallback silently reproduced the collapse-to-zero defect on the first show of every night; entering early left the resting playback unsupervised through the lead window; a clock jump could satisfy the hold and time out every barrier cue at once; and `enterResting` evaluated a launch barrier it does not have.

**The F0 finding that reshaped the track, and the owner decision it produced.** Stock FPP has no brightness command; the owner decided (RES-018, Linear SM-49) on a ShowMesh-owned FPP component with two independently owned values rather than trusting FPP's destructive absolute-brightness write. None of that component is built. F4 as built implements no brightness fade, and readiness rejects a configuration that needs one.

**Decisions made.** The brightness question (RES-018, Linear SM-49) is the owner's; every other decision below is an **orchestrator ruling made in this session**, not an owner decision, and is labelled as such here because five code comments in the branch had mislabelled orchestrator rulings as owner rulings and were corrected during review:

- Same-show enforcement (F1) is extended to `timelineAsset` and every background-audio item, not only cue actions.
- Structurally unverifiable readiness checks get their own state and are excluded from the readiness aggregate, so `ready` stays reachable rather than permanently blocked by a check that cannot run.
- Pre-show starts the resting playlist with repeat enabled: the reference day's 4:30 PM pre-show against a five-minute resting FSEQ would otherwise leave twenty-five minutes of dark house.
- Show-launch replacement (F3) is conditional on positive instance/name/evidence identification rather than on FPP simply being busy.
- A dispatch with no attributed principal is refused (found reachable through a restart during preshow in F3).
- `RoleScheduler` gains `night:command`, without which ADR-038's own actor could not invoke ADR-038's own vocabulary.
- `end-session` is added as a provisional operator recovery action (F2) that abandons a degraded session, reaches `stopped`, and launches nothing; it deliberately does not clear the degraded flag and continue, since resuming a session whose real state cannot be confirmed is the guess ADR-038 forbids. Provisional pending the owner's ruling on whether an operator recovery verb belongs inside ADR-038's closed lifecycle vocabulary (Linear SM-82, open).

**Questions raised with the owner:**

- Linear SM-49 (brightness): stock FPP has no brightness-shaped, non-destructive control; the owner decided on a ShowMesh-owned FPP component with two independently owned values (RES-018). **Answered.**
- Linear SM-82: whether `end-session`, an operator recovery verb, sits inside ADR-038's closed command vocabulary. **Open**, and `end-session` ships provisionally in F2 pending the ruling.
- Linear SM-48: whether a `show.action` can declare its own idempotence, raised by F4's recovery-path work on non-idempotent action rejection. **Open.**

**Deferred:**

- F5, audio integration, is blocked on Track C's `pkg/audio` reaching `main`. The wire contract is pinned in F1 and has already moved once; the block is the merge landing, not the design.
- F6, optional power/thermal/interlock integration. F1 rejects the `siteControl` and `interlocks` configuration blocks outright with a problem naming F6, rather than accepting configuration nothing yet enforces.
- F8, integrated and failure verification against the acceptance scenarios in `RESTING-MODE.md`.
- F4's own `make test-integration` run had not happened at the time of writing (see Verification gates).

**Verification gates**, run by the orchestrating session on the folded tree, one seam at a time, never by the builders themselves:

- `make check` exit 0 on each of F0 through F3.
- `make test-integration`, each with an isolated broker container and port: F1 `ok github.com/showmeshsystems/showmesh/test/integration 287.957s`, zero failures; F2 `ok ... 292.492s`, 74 passed, zero failures; F3 `ok ... 298.666s`, zero failures.
- `make test-integration-fpp` on F3: `ok ... 176.682s`, 29 cases. The FPP primitive suite had been seen to flake at host load average 106 during the same session and was correctly flagged rather than asserted away; it passed clean at load 51.
- F4, after its second review round: `make check` exit 0; `make test-integration` `ok ... 303.774s`, zero failures. This gate was deliberately deferred twice while host load sat between 80 and 167 with several parallel sessions running, and run only once the machine was quiet, because this project has already recorded that a loaded host produces failures that are plausible, unrelated to the diff, and different on each run.

**What this track may not claim.** Everything in this session is built against fakes, a throwaway bench `fppd`, and F0's recorded observations. Nothing ran against the deployed fleet. `TRACK-F-resting-mode.md`'s own acceptance section says unit tests alone cannot complete this track; that remains true after this session. Linear SM-50, SM-51, and SM-66 carry the hardware-dependent verification items this track cannot close on this machine.

### Addendum, 2026-08-21: merged to `main` at `ba9dc38`, and the three defects the first green build found

**Merged with all eleven checks green.** `make check` exit 0 and `./scripts/test-integration.sh` 128 passes on the merged tree, plus CI across both Go versions, all four integration jobs, lint, ui, vuln, docker and the FPP bench suite.

**Getting CI to build at all took ten fixes**, listed above and completed here. Two more were found after that entry was written. **Matrix `fail-fast` was cancelling the 1.26.6 leg** on every failure, so a run reported one failure where it could have reported two, and each hidden one cost a full round trip; that leg then produced the cleanest evidence for the position defect. And **a single large `apt-get install` was observed exiting 0 having installed `libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev` but not `libgstreamer1.0-dev`**, in a run where the identical command had installed it before, surfacing several steps and one seven-minute `fppd` build later as `pkg-config` resolving nothing. The cgo dependencies now install in their own call and are verified immediately, so a missing one fails where it happened and names itself.

**Three defects were then found by CI actually running the engine, and all three are fixed here.**

**A branch reported position from the decode frontier rather than from playback.** `queryPosition` read `decodebin.QueryPosition`. `decodebin` is a `GstBin`, and a position query on a bin is resolved by GStreamer's bin and pad forwarding, which on this flat topology, where every branch element is a direct sibling of the shared mixers in one pipeline, can be answered on the shared pipeline's timeline. Measured reporting 5.04 s against a 4 s engine uptime, and 4 s past a named start position of 0 s. It now queries `volume`, which is branch-local.

**The first fix for that was rejected in review, and it is the more useful half of the story.** It derived position arithmetically as `segmentStart + pipelineRunningTime() - mixerOffset`. The arithmetic was self-consistent, its concurrency was independently verified complete, and it made both failing tests pass. It was still wrong, because every term was a value the package had written from its own arguments: the expression had no data dependency on `filesrc`, `decodebin`, the queue or the mixer, so it could not disagree with the code's own intent, and a seek returning true without moving the stream would have reported the requested position forever. **Two existing tests measured that loss of power directly**: the LTC back-pressure check returned exactly `1.0000` by construction and its empirically calibrated run-ahead bound read `~0`, so a regression halving the program rate or doubling the queue cap would have been invisible. Against a real query the same tests read 1.0230 and 1.0153, and 259 ms and 257 ms inside a band whose edges were measured at 219 ms and 298 ms. **A derived value that replaces an observation stops being evidence, and the tests that depended on it stop being tests.**

**`Load` was starved rather than slow.** `go test -race ./...` schedules all 45 package binaries on a four-core runner, and `internal/coordinator/api`'s race suite alone runs 570 to 780 seconds. The failure landed on a different set of tests every run, which is the tell. The engine package now runs alone, first, in its own step, and **no timeout was widened**. Two guards travel with the split because a split creates two new ways to pass while covering nothing: every engine test is behind `//go:build cgo`, and **`go test` on a package whose files are all excluded prints `ok` and exits 0**, measured at 8 ms with one surviving test file out of eleven, so the step whose whole purpose is proving the engine works could have ticked green over an empty set; and the second step's exclusion is `grep -vx` on the full import path, because an unanchored match would also exclude a future sibling that the first step's pattern would not pick up, leaving it tested by neither. That is the same silent-skip shape `scripts/test-integration-fpp.sh` already guards against.

**A restarted broker was called ready as soon as a port accepted.** `TestLocalAudioSessionSurvivesBrokerLoss` failed two of its three CI runs on `CONNECT: EOF` and `connection reset by peer`. A container's published port is served by Docker's port proxy the instant the mapping exists, which says nothing about whether Mosquitto behind it will serve a session. Readiness now comes from a real MQTT CONNECT retried under a bound matching the client it gates. Review then caught that the first version of that fix **turned a deterministic auth refusal into a fifteen-second timeout carrying an empty message**, because paho returns both the CONNACK and a non-nil error on reason codes 0x80 and above and its message carries only the broker's usually-empty reason string; the code is now read off the ack, and 0x85, 0x86 and 0x87 fail immediately, because a broker that answered and refused made a decision rather than reporting a readiness state.

**Two claims were withdrawn rather than left standing.** The position defect was filed as "a cue plays from the middle of its file", an audible show defect; the audio was always correct and only the reported number was wrong, which is still serious because position drives the operator surface, the inter-item gap and seek re-anchoring, but nobody would have heard it. And the distinct `Load`-timeout sentinel was reported as fixing a misclassification; review established that a timed-out `Load` never classified as a decode failure, since `ClassifyFault` returns `FaultOther` for anything not wrapping one of six sentinels and `context.DeadlineExceeded` wraps none. The change is a readability improvement guarding a future regression, and is recorded as that.

**Unchanged by any of this: nothing has produced sound.** Every sink in every test is `fakesink`. No real ALSA, no multichannel hardware, no channel discreteness, no program-to-LTC alignment. Track C's fifteen acceptance criteria remain unobserved on an assembled path.

Review verified independently rather than by reading: the UNIQUE partial index backing atomicity is real and its firing was reproduced; the no-duplicate-current-row claim holds under a second cycle form the builder had not considered, where after a rollback the current row has an older `created_at` than the row it supersedes, so any newest-wins ordering would pick the wrong row (there is none); the rollback reaches nodes, traced through to the agent's `os.Rename`. One blocking finding, fixed: `POST /assets`'s OpenAPI operation description still claimed re-uploading identical bytes is always idempotent with no new row, so the public contract had drifted from the already-corrected CLI help — no gate reads prose. `AssetUpload.tsx` had no test file at all; three were added and mutation-verified.

Now refused with 409, matching the existing `fppcommand` behavior. Review attacked the params-comparison claim and produced a stronger form: the old bare `json.Marshal` and the new `canonicalParamsJSON` emit byte-identical output for every map this dispatch path can construct, so no stored idempotency key is invalidated by the upgrade, and neither shipped client can trigger the new 409 because both mint a fresh key per call. One finding fixed: the replay path wrote no audit entry while its own comment claimed it mirrored `resolveFPPCommandReplay` (which does write one) — the gap on replay was pre-existing and the gap on the new conflict refusal was introduced by this seam.

That premise did not survive measurement. Verified end to end on a freshly bootstrapped coordinator, isolated port and data dir, driven entirely through `showmeshctl`: zero-to-one, rotate, absent-key-keeps, `--clear-password`, zero-to-one again, all worked with no restart; `GET` reports `passwordSet` only; the plaintext is absent from `showmesh.db` and its WAL, searched in the raw files. All three of decision 7's rules already hold. The only real difference from decision 7's text is that the secret lives in a 0600 file on the data volume rather than inside SQLite, and decision 7's consequence paragraph already says "volume," which the file is on. The distinguishing failure mode was tested directly: with the secret file removed and the revision still recording `passwordSet`, `GET` reports "not set," because the handler reads live presence rather than the revision's own claim — it degrades honestly. Nothing was reworked. One test was added, for the explicit empty-string clear (the one write-surface meaning the existing suite never asserted). The builder stopped rather than minting a schema version to satisfy the brief as written, which is why this was caught rather than shipped. Returned to the owner as Linear SM-59.

**The lesson from this session, and it is about the parallel-session rules rather than about E7.** E7-3 added a refusal to a write path that had previously accepted anything, and the branch's own gates were green: `make check`, `go test -race ./...`, two Opus reviews, and an orchestrator acceptance run against a running coordinator. **`make test-integration` then failed on the first try**, because `test/integration` writes a `show.action` naming `bench-show` and never creates that show. The refusal was correct and the fixture predated it. About a dozen unit tests had been updated with the prerequisite; the integration suite was outside anything a builder is permitted to run, since CLAUDE.md's multi-track rule keeps builders out of it to avoid the Mosquitto container and port collision, so **no gate the builder could execute could have reached it.** That is the standing cost of the rule, and it is why the orchestrator runs that suite before a merge rather than after one. The general form is one this project already knows in a different disguise: when you turn a permissive path into a refusing one, enumerate what becomes unreachable, and test fixtures are part of what becomes unreachable. The fix swept the whole suite rather than the one failing line, found two write sites, and put the prerequisite in a shared `ensureShow` helper in `harness_test.go` so the next fixture author has a precedent to copy rather than a pattern to rediscover.

**And the second half of that story is the opposite error, caught by a control run rather than by an argument.** After the fixture fix, the next integration run failed again, on two different FPP tests, with reasons of the form `fpp.status is paused, want "idle"`. Those look exactly like a real regression in the command confirmation path. They are not. Four runs produced **four disjoint failure sets**, no test failed twice, and the decisive run was `make test-integration` on **unmodified `main`**, which also failed, on a fifth test, with `POST /api/v1/fpp/.../commands: EOF`, meaning the coordinator process died mid-request. The mechanism: `showmesh-bench-fpp-master` is a single shared container holding real playlist state, driven by every worktree's integration run, and the script isolates the Mosquitto container and port but has no equivalent isolation for the bench `fppd`. A concurrent run from another session was directly confirmed in the process table during one of them. **One evening produced both error directions this project warns about**: a genuine regression that could have been dismissed as flake, and contention noise that could have been chased as a regression. The discipline that separated them was not judgement, it was running the same suite on unmodified `main`. Filed as Linear SM-87 with the recommendation to give the bench `fppd` the same per-run isolation Mosquitto already has.

**Addendum, 2026-08-19: three dedicated per-PR reviews, run after this session's seams were already built and gated, found eleven further defects, four of them merge blockers.** They replaced an earlier bundled review that read all three PRs (E7, asset rollback, render idempotency) in one pass; the bundled pass produced six findings, of which only two held up, plus scrambled bookkeeping. The owner's own conclusion, recorded here because it is the reason the per-PR reviews were run at all: reviewing three unrelated PRs in one sitting was itself the mistake. Everything below **corrects and extends** the "Completed" bullets above rather than replacing them; each earlier bullet's review record stands for what it found at the time, not for the last word on that PR.

- **PR #19 (Track E seam E7), four blockers, all fixed:**
  - Action invocation could not pin an action revision, so a Track F cue queued against revision 3 would execute revision 4 if an operator activated it first in between. Idempotency prevented duplication but not meaning. Fixed with an optional `requestedRevision` on the invocation request; the response always states which revision actually ran.
  - Restart and replay could not preserve a truthful result, in four distinct ways: degraded attribution was not persisted, a failed outcome journal still returned a resolved result, reconciliation overwrote a durable confirmed FPP child with `unconfirmed`, and reconciliation only ran once at coordinator startup.
  - MQTT's precise outcome state was discarded, so the same underlying action failure recorded its reason when run through a macro and recorded nothing when triggered by a direct invocation.
  - Idempotency replay compared only the target id and never the command family, so a command from a different family that happened to collide on the same key returned its own unrelated result as a successful replay. Reproduced with `status = 200, want 409`.
  - Three further, non-blocking correctness defects also found in PR #19: a Resolume-only binding check returned `500` when an unrelated FPP inventory lookup failed; both MQTT implementations could report a dispatch that never reached the wire; and comment discipline still carried review history and test narration after three prior cleanup passes on this same code.
- **PR #17 (asset rollback), two blockers, both fixed:** the rollback audit recorded the asset that was restored but not the one it displaced, and the audit timestamp was captured before the bytes finished streaming, so it could predate the actual state change by the entire upload duration and misorder concurrent transitions. A third instance of the same timestamp-before-the-work defect was found by the builder, not by the review: the response's `serverTime` used the same stale value, so a response could report a `createdAt` newer than its own `serverTime`.
- **PR #18 (render idempotency), one blocker, and it corrected the filed issue as much as the code.** The filed fix, "look the idempotency key up before resolving params," was itself insufficient: render dispatch stores resolved wire parameters and never retained the caller's original `sequenceId`, so an early lookup keyed on action and node alone would have let a genuinely different sequence replay as a false success. Trading a false `409` for a false confirmation is worse. Fixed by durably retaining a canonical caller-request identity and checking it before any mutable resolution, keeping the existing UNIQUE insert as the concurrency authority.

**Two owner rulings came out of the PR #19 review, both 2026-08-19.** The empty-string `outcome` broke ADR-020 for any client that is not this project's own: the CLI and UI silently repaired the blank, but an independent v1 client has no such repair and no contract basis for one. It is replaced by an explicit `pending`/`resolved` lifecycle state, with the existing five outcome words reserved for resolved results only. Separately, `show:action:invoke` is ruled umbrella authority rather than conjunctive with the per-integration scopes (`fpp:command`, `resolume:action`); the code already behaved that way, and IDENTIFIER-REGISTER had recorded the opposite, which means the register was describing a security property the code did not actually have.

**A punch-list item closed.** The PR #17 review drove a genuine xLights FSEQ from A to B and back to A through the real coordinator, CLI, Mosquitto, agent, HTTP fetch, rename and inventory, measured end to end at 55.641s. This retires the standing caveat that no real xLights FSEQ had ever been uploaded (carried in this file's Current state block as of 2026-08-17, now stale on that point), and it exercised the exact case the rollback design turns on: A and B sharing one runtime filename. The run was loopback, so the real-network-link half of that caveat is not retired and remains SM-18.

**The lesson this addendum exists to record.** Eleven defects survived four earlier review passes on this same code, and the misses were not random: every one was invisible from a single-request read of a diff. Durability and recovery across a restart, a key namespace shared between command families, a timestamp taken before the work it timestamps, and a stored value that was derived rather than original are all properties of the system over time, not of one call in isolation. The earlier passes read each change as a sequence of individual calls, which is exactly the frame those defects hide from; the dedicated per-PR sessions had room to model the system over time instead. Two of the eleven were caught only because the tests written for them were checked to fail first: reintroducing the exact defect a PR had just fixed left the entire package tree green, and an assertion meant for one boolean was silently satisfied by a different flag. This stands alongside the existing "a test's name is a claim" lesson from Step 3, not as a new one.

**Decisions made:** none rising to a new ADR this session. ADR-028 decision 10 (owner, 2026-08-17, already recorded in the ADR and in `docs/decisions/README.md`) is now implemented by the asset-rollback branch above. No decision was made or superseded regarding `fpp.mqtt`; the owner's 2026-08-17 ruling stands unimplemented pending SM-59. Two further rulings, both owner, both 2026-08-19, recorded in the addendum above: the invocation outcome field gains an explicit `pending`/`resolved` lifecycle state (ADR-020 conformance for third-party clients), and `show:action:invoke` is confirmed umbrella authority over the per-integration scopes, correcting IDENTIFIER-REGISTER rather than the code.

## 2026-08-18 (Track C seams C6 and C7: session telemetry, fault containment, and the follow-up fix)

**Goal:** ship session telemetry, readiness, and command outcomes (C6) and failure containment plus manual recovery (C7) on `track-c/audio-node`, built together because C7's faults are only observable through C6's evidence.

**Completed:** all recorded in [TRACK-C-audio-node.md](TRACK-C-audio-node.md)'s "C6 and C7, complete 2026-08-18" section.

- **`9e613d7`:** eighteen `audio_session.*` signals under the reserved `audio_session` resource kind; one new node-level signal, `node.audio.clock.alignment` (the twelfth `node.audio.*` signal), which reports `not_collected` with a reason always — nothing in this seam measures program-to-LTC alignment, and `TestClockAlignmentAlwaysNotCollected` fails if the signal is ever made to look measured; six named fault classes (plus `none` and `other`) that never collapse into `stopped` or into each other, clearing only on a successful `prepare` since that is the one choke point every `prepare`/`start`/`advance`/restore-time revalidation passes through (`TestFaultClearsOnlyOnRevalidation`, `TestRestartRevalidatesRatherThanBlindlyCarryingAFault`); and the manual recovery procedure at [AUDIO-ENGINE.md §11.4](../architecture/AUDIO-ENGINE.md), required by ADR-019's removal of automatic fallback. Two defects fixed beyond the seam's own stated scope, both in `internal/agent/audio/mix.go`: the fade-completion read's error path was previously unclassified (a real backend erroring there produced no fault); and fade completion compared reported gain to target with exact float equality, which a real ramp backend would miss by floating-point error (`0.19999999999999998` vs. a `0.2` target) and report `unconfirmable` forever — now a `1e-6`-tolerance comparison, mutation-verified by `TestFadeCompletionToleratesFloatingPointDrift`.
- **`84c4865`:** a single-media session (no playlist) never completed — `advanceLocked` refused unconditionally with no playlist, and the natural-completion watcher calls that same method, so a finished single-asset session reported `state=playing` forever at its full-duration position, measured unchanged for 25+ seconds; fixed so an unforced advance completes a single-media session the way a playlist running off its end with `RepeatNone` does (`TestNaturalCompletionOfASingleMediaSession`). A content-hash mismatch had been classified as `media_disappeared`; it is now its own fault, `media_mismatch` (`TestMediaMismatchFaultDistinctFromDisappeared`), since the asset being absent and the asset being present-with-wrong-content send an operator to different places — AUDIO-ENGINE.md §11.4 updated accordingly. Two defects in the broker-loss integration test itself: commands dispatched before the agent's subscribe completed (dropped, not delayed — every other test in the package calls the documented warm-up barrier first, this one hadn't), and the test's own observer had no reconnect after the broker container restarted.

**Review findings:** the C6/C7 defects above were found by the builder chasing a reproducibly-failing new integration test, not by a separate review pass. Two new LESSONS.md entries: "A test must exercise the ordinary case, not only the elaborate one" and "A defect that only a real backend can produce, hidden by a fake that is too clean."

**Decisions made:** none rising to an ADR this session. `media_mismatch` is a new fault-vocabulary member, not a durable architectural constraint, and is recorded in `pkg/audio/fault.go` and AUDIO-ENGINE.md §11.4 rather than a new ADR.

## 2026-08-17 (Track B PR #14: three external-review findings fixed and folded on `track-b/integration`)

**Goal:** fold the three findings from an external review of PR #14 (`track-b/integration`) back into the branch, and re-run the gates the review specified.

**Completed:**

- **`IdleOutputDiagnostic` no longer draws two greys.** The prior implementation satisfied "generated, never frozen" literally but minimally: a uniform field alternating between two grey values at 0.5 Hz reads as a plausible frozen picture on a dark wall. Replaced with a vertical bar swept across a constant non-black background. Position derives from the tick's wall-clock time rather than an incrementing counter, so the bar is itself a clock: a stalled writer produces a stalled bar rather than one that resumes smoothly and hides the gap. Drawing is erase-and-redraw (cost proportional to bar width times height, independent of surface width) rather than a full-buffer rewrite, which at a 1080p-equivalent matrix would be roughly 6.2 MB per frame and 249 MB/s at 40 fps spent on an idle screen, against RES-004's roughly 14% spare on one thread. The ADR-040 boundary (ShowMesh may extract/generate, GStreamer owns frames) is argued in the code comment: every byte written is one of two constants at a computed offset, a fill rather than a render, with no content byte read, scaled, or blended. Two tests were added and mutation-verified by the orchestrator independently of the builder: the buffer changes between ticks, and the bar advances by exactly the expected number of columns between two known time samples.
- **The Operator UI's O(M) client-side fan-out is gone.** `RenderSurfacePanel` listed `show.surface` summaries then issued one detail fetch per row purely to filter by node. Replaced with a server-side `?node=` filter on the existing list endpoint (the review's preferred Shape A, consistent with ADR-014's rule against one-off endpoints) — the per-row calls are removed, not reduced. A `?node=` filter passed to a config kind with no node concept is refused with a problem naming the kind, never silently ignored, because a quietly dropped filter would let a client act on a set it did not ask for.
- **`render_kill_test.go`'s comment no longer claims a guarantee it doesn't need.** The prior comment argued that a 100 ms report interval structurally guarantees the transient `restarting` state lands in a report — sound, but attached to the wrong thing, since the test's actual verdict is steady state (`restart_count >= 1` plus the surface returning to `running` on evidence post-dating the kill). The comment now scopes the structural claim to the transient indicator and states what actually decides pass/fail.
- **The 100 ms report interval is kept, and the stated reasoning for keeping it was corrected.** The review proposed 500 ms and characterized 1:1 sampling as a coin flip. That framing was off: a window of length T sampled every T is pigeonhole-guaranteed to be caught by a clean periodic ticker, so the real objection is zero jitter margin, not a coin flip. Measured: 30 runs at 500 ms all passed, including under synthetic CPU load. 100 ms is kept for jitter margin, and the comment now says so rather than asserting correctness was ever at stake.

**Decisions made:** none rising to an ADR; all three findings and the interval reasoning are recorded above and in the code comments they correct, not restated elsewhere.

**Questions raised with the owner:** none this session.

**A measurement worth recording as a lesson.** The 20-run stability check the review asked for was run twice; the first run's result was wrong because of how it was run, not what it measured. First attempt: 5 of 20 passed, all five failures traced to shared-host infrastructure (a builder's Mosquitto container still bound to the port the loop used, host load average 62 from concurrent agents) — `port is already allocated`, a process killed externally, a container vanishing mid-run. Zero assertion failures, zero transient-wait timeouts. Second attempt, after removing stray containers, waiting for load to fall, and using an isolated port: 20 of 20 passed. The generalizable point runs in both directions: earlier the same day a builder attributed a real regression to shared-host flake, and here the orchestrator nearly attributed healthy behavior to a flaky test. The discipline is the same either way — isolate the container name and port, remove leftovers, re-run, and read *why* each failure happened rather than counting them. A failure that moves between runs is a tell, not a verdict.

**Deferred:**

- Nothing has run on real render hardware or against a real FPP player driving a wall; Track B's acceptance criteria 2 and 6 remain open, and criterion 1's Operator UI half remains unverified in a browser. These stay on `docs/private/PUNCH-LIST.md`.
- `render.settings.restartPolicy` remains configurable and ignored: it is Supervisor-scoped rather than surface-scoped and needs its own distribution mechanism. Owner decision, not made this session.
- The FSEQ's own step time is still never reconciled against the surface's configured `frameRate`. Owner decision (refuse, or trust the file), not made this session.
- The merge to `main` and the Track G rebase are a separate session; this branch is deliberately not rebased here.
- [TRACK-B-RENDER-NODE.md](../bench/TRACK-B-RENDER-NODE.md) was written this session: the procedure for the real-hardware render bench that closes the two open acceptance criteria above.

**Verification gates**, run by the orchestrating session on the folded tree, in the order the review specified: `go build ./...` exit 0; `go test -race ./...` exit 0, 33 packages, zero failures; `make check` exit 0; `make test-integration` exit 0, `ok github.com/showmeshsystems/showmesh/test/integration 289.322s`, zero failures; plus the isolated 20-run stability check on the kill test, second attempt: 20/20. **Not run:** anything against real render hardware, a real FPP player, or a real Resolume/wall. No claim in this entry rests on hardware evidence that was not captured.

## 2026-08-17 (Track B: pipeline supervision, FSEQ extraction, NDI output, capability advertisement — built and gated, not yet merged)

**Goal:** build the render node past B0's transport spike and B1's stub agent: real GStreamer pipeline supervision, MultiSync-driven FSEQ extraction, NDI output, and capability advertisement, per [TRACK-B-BUILD-CONTRACT.md](TRACK-B-BUILD-CONTRACT.md) and [ADR-040](../decisions/ADR-040-renderer-extracts-channels-gstreamer-owns-frames.md).

**Completed:** seams B2 (`internal/agent/pipeline`, the `Supervisor`, bounded-backoff restart, `render.surface.apply|clear`, `render.pipeline.restart`), B2b (coordinator dispatch endpoints, `render:command` scope, `showmeshctl render status|apply|clear|restart`, Operator UI render controls and dashboard attention items, an end-to-end integration test against a real agent), B2c (`render.settings`, store-backed and revisioned per ADR-039, applying without a restart per ADR-036), B3 (`pkg/fseq`, a pure-Go FSEQ v2 reader; the agent's own MultiSync listener and `Timeline`; the frame writer extracting the surface's channel range from the local FSEQ at the timeline's reported frame and writing it to the pipeline's stdin), B4 (the NDI sink stage, `render.transport.probe` driving a real state transition rather than trusting element presence, `showmeshctl render transport`), and B5 (real capability detection replacing `SHOWMESH_NODE_CAPABILITIES` as the only source, `render.surface` and `transport.ndi.send` advertised independently and only from evidence). [RES-017](../research/RES-017-fseq-format.md) (the FSEQ v2 format, researched from real per-target files) and [ADR-040](../decisions/ADR-040-renderer-extracts-channels-gstreamer-owns-frames.md) (the ADR-007 per-frame boundary, narrowed to name FSEQ extraction as ShowMesh-owned and everything past it as GStreamer's) were both drafted this track and accepted by the owner 2026-08-17. All work is on `track-b/integration` at `b1789ac` and has not been folded to `main`.

**Decisions made:** ADR-040 (owner, 2026-08-17), narrowing ADR-007 to say ShowMesh may open, parse, and extract from the FSEQ, and must not touch a frame past that point. Ruling 3's idle-output default (`black`) confirmed by the owner 2026-08-17 with one refinement: `diagnostic` must be generated content, never a held frame, because a still picture on a house is indistinguishable from a crashed renderer, which is the exact failure `diagnostic` exists to surface. Both recorded in the build contract and in ADR-040 rather than restated here.

**Full-track review, after every seam's own `make check` and `make test-integration` were already green, found 21 findings plus 2 more in a `pkg/fseq`-focused addendum.** All 23 are fixed at `b1789ac`. The reviewer's own framing: *every mechanism this track built to prove a frame reached the wall reports success, or a plausible zero, in the exact case where it did not.*

The two worst:

- **Nothing reported whether a surface was drawing content or holding idle black.** With the MultiSync listener unable to bind UDP 32320, the timeline correctly stayed `unknown`, which the build contract's ruling 3 correctly routes to the idle output (`black` by default) — that part worked as specified. What was missing is that the node's own render report carried no signal distinguishing that case from real playback: `pipelineState: running`, frames climbing at 40/s, zero late, zero dropped, rate 40.0, identical in every field to a surface actually rendering the show. A green dashboard and a black wall were indistinguishable from the coordinator's evidence, all night. The build contract itself warns about exactly this shape of failure (ruling 5: "the process is up" is not "frames are arriving somewhere") and the shipped code produced precisely that gap on the timeline side rather than the pipeline-liveness side the contract's own example names.
- **The fast-failure lockout meant to catch a crash-looping pipeline was dead code.** It reset `consecutiveFailures` on the stdout string `"Setting pipeline to PLAYING"`, which `gst-launch` prints *before* attempting the state change, not after. Reproduced by hand on this machine against real `gst-launch-1.0`: the marker prints, the pipeline errors roughly 70 ms later, and the process exits 1 — so a pipeline that fails identically and immediately on every restart printed the marker every time and `consecutiveFailures` never left zero. Fixed by keying the reset to `"New clock:"`, which only appears after a successful transition, verified against both a succeeding and a forced-failing real pipeline.

A third, more severe class from the `pkg/fseq` addendum: **a corrupt FSEQ could OOM-kill the agent.** A `uint32` underflow in the block table (`firstFrame` never validated against `frameCount`) wrapped on a bad entry, and the decode-size bound takes the max across all blocks, so one corrupt entry poisoned the whole file's bound — a file whose correct bound is the 64 MiB floor produced a computed zstd memory limit of 9,665,488,683,008 bytes, and `Open` succeeded regardless. This is reachable by corruption alone, not only malice, and it sits on the boot-resume path that exists precisely for when no coordinator is reachable to supply a fresh file. Compounding it, the pre-decode size check read only the first zstd frame of a block while `DecodeAll` loops over every frame in it, and an existing test asserted the check was correct while only ever constructing single-frame blocks.

**Also fixed**, recorded here rather than restated in TRACK-B (link, don't restate): `render.surface.apply` could confirm off the pipeline it was in the process of killing; `framesRate` froze at its last good value forever once frames stopped, rather than reporting the staleness; the late/dropped counters never used the tick time they were handed, so they could not see missed ticks; `SetStepTime` was never called in production despite a comment claiming it was, so the timeline ran permanently at the 25 ms default regardless of the FSEQ's own step time; a failed boot resume reported nothing at all; a rejected `apply` overwrote the last known-good persisted assignment before validating the new one; the coordinator discarded the node's own evidence timestamp and substituted its own receipt time (the fourth time this project has made that specific ADR-011 mistake); six error paths dispatched `"params": null` and reported a coordinator store failure as if the node had rejected the command; capability advertisement claimed pixel formats the renderer refuses, and a large-enough claim could consume the node's entire advertisement budget so it published no hello at all and vanished from inventory; `render.transport.probe` was implemented and wired to nothing that could call it before this review.

**Questions raised with the owner:** two, both 2026-08-17, both answered and recorded above and in ADR-040/the build contract rather than here — the ADR-007 boundary (ADR-040) and the idle-output diagnostic-mode refinement (ruling 3).

**Deferred:** the two acceptance criteria that need real hardware — see Current state above and TRACK-B's own status. Recovery behavior (sender/receiver surviving each other's restart) stays unverified; B0's spike run 5 never ran and nothing in this session ran it either.

**Verification gates.** Run by the orchestrator personally on the final commit `b1789ac`: `go build ./...` exit 0; `go test -race ./...` exit 0, 33 packages, zero failures; `make check` exit 0; `make test-integration` exit 0, `ok github.com/showmeshsystems/showmesh/test/integration 274.218s`, zero failures. **Not run:** anything against real render hardware, a real FPP player, or a real Resolume/wall. No claim in this entry rests on hardware evidence that was not captured.

**One lesson beyond the pattern above, worth carrying past this track:** three of the twenty-three findings lived in the seam between two individually-correct, individually-green changes rather than in either change alone — a fix for a two-node surface-id collision removed the property that made clear-confirmation work, which a review had verified as safe roughly an hour earlier; a test assertion that was correct when written became wrong once a legitimately-`not_collected` signal was added later; and a correct `ObservedAt` fence was sound only because of an invariant a different, concurrent seam was violating. See [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) for this and three more that generalize past Track B.

## 2026-08-16 (B0, the NDI transport spike, run on the owner's bench and passed)

**Goal:** fold the owner's overnight NDI spike result into the record, and establish what it does and does not license.

**Completed:** documentation only, no code. The spike itself was owner bench work.

The measurement: **982,100 frames rendered, 0 dropped, 0 late, 0 errors, `current: 40.00 average: 40.00`, over 6 h 49 min continuous**, ending 23:32 on 2026-08-16 and still clean when stopped. Renderer node a Dell OptiPlex Micro 7050 (Core i7, 16 GB, 256 GB M.2) on bare-metal Debian 13, canvas 1920x1080 UYVY at 40 fps, wired Ethernet to the core switch on a UniFi fabric with NDI enabled, GStreamer NDI plugin compiled from `gst-plugins-rs` on the node. **Two receivers attached for the duration**, Resolume Arena displaying and NDI Video Monitor on a second machine, neither reporting a drop or an error.

Records updated: [RES-006](../research/RES-006-linux-ndi-support.md) (open item 1 discharged, status to L2 for the amd64 sender, packaging check answered, two new open items), [RES-005](../research/RES-005-ndi-vs-hdmi-transport.md) (L2 for single-surface wired NDI stability and pacing, explicit list of criteria still L0), [RES-004](../research/RES-004-virtual-matrix-renderer-performance.md) (stays L0, with the reason stated), the [research tracker](../research/README.md), [Track B](TRACK-B-nodes-and-projection.md) (B0 marked done, B4 unblocked), and the punch list.

**Decisions made.** Two, both the owner's, both 2026-08-16.

**The NDI plugin is compiled from source and that is accepted for day-0.** The Debian 13 packaging check the spike doc demanded was run and returned no: no usable packaged element could be located, and the source build was four steps. The downsides are understood and accepted (a cargo toolchain on the node, a `.so` with no distribution provenance, a rebuild to redo between seasons); the mitigation is a scripted build. **Node build mechanics are owner work outside the build sessions.** This spends one of the three arguments RES-006 used to prefer Debian over RHEL-family, since ShowMesh now owns that cargo build anyway; the two structural arguments (FPP is Debian-based, Raspberry Pi OS is Debian) are untouched and are why Debian stands.

**1920x1080 is recorded as a tested dimension, not a ceiling.** Day-0 intent is roughly one 1080p-equivalent surface per node across three nodes, portrait 1080x1920 in practice at the same pixel count, which is about a 1.5x pixel increase over last season. RES-004's treatment of pixel count as a test parameter is unchanged, and hardware determines what a given show can run.

**Questions raised with the owner:** four, and the fourth turned out to matter more than the three that prompted it.

Three were about whether the result meant what it looked like. Canvas dimensions, because 40 fps means nothing without the pixel count. Whether the sink ran `sync=true`, because with QoS disabled `dropped: 0` is structurally zero rather than measured. And whether Resolume was actually attached, because an NDI sender runs perfectly happily with nobody listening. Answers: 1920x1080, yes, and yes plus a second independent receiver.

The fourth was CPU utilisation, asked because RES-004's renderer has to fit in whatever the encode leaves. **The answer was 86% of one core, load average `0.58 0.30 0.38`, and it changed the shape of the result rather than confirming it.** The spike's pipeline has no `queue`, so generation, encode and send shared one streaming thread; the box was near idle while that one thread ran at 86%. **The ceiling is per-core, not per-machine**, so a node reporting itself 85% idle will drop frames when that thread passes 100%. Three design inputs for B2 and B3 fall straight out of it and are recorded in RES-004: put a `queue` between renderer and sink so the idle cores are reachable, emit UYVY natively because the measurement was taken on the zero-conversion path, and treat pixel count as spending a thread budget with 14% spare rather than a machine budget with 75% spare. The load averages are **not** steady-state figures: the one-minute value sits above the five and fifteen minute values, which means load was still climbing when the sample was taken, so the 0.38 must not be read as a soak average.

The source pattern was bars plus snow. **No further spike bench time is being spent characterising the encode against synthetic patterns; B0 passed and is closed** (owner, 2026-08-16). The measurement that decides RES-004 is B3 rendering real content through the same path, not another test pattern.

**Deferred.** Spike run 5 (recovery) not run. The plugin build recipe is unrecorded and exists only on the bench machine. The `videotestsrc` pattern is unresolved, which is what qualifies the 86% CPU figure. `arm64` and the Ubuntu 24.04 release target remain RES-006 open items. All on the punch list.

**Verification gates:** none run. This session changed documentation only and touched no code, so `make check` and `make test-integration` were not re-run and no claim here rests on them.

**One thing worth carrying, and it is the reverse of this project's usual lesson.** The first read of this result argued against it on the strength of the average frame rate, which is genuinely near-unfalsifiable: `videotestsrc is-live=true` into a `sync=true` sink is clocked to 40 fps, so 40.00 is roughly what that pipeline prints whether or not the far side is coping. That was the right thing to distrust and the wrong thing to lead with, because the operator already had the number that settled it. **`dropped: 0` across 982,100 consecutive frames on a QoS-active sink is a measurement; the average is close to a tautology.** The harness says exactly this in its own summary output (`run-spike.sh:262`, "min and p05 are the numbers that matter. Report them, not the mean"), which is worth remembering the next time a bench result arrives as a headline figure: ask which number in it could have come out differently.

## 2026-08-17 (Track G: operator surface parity, specified and built in one session)

**Goal:** the owner could not connect Resolume Arena to the running test stack from any operator surface. Find out why, audit whether it was one variable or a pattern, and close it.

**What it turned out to be.** `SHOWMESH_RESOLUME_URL` is an environment variable read once at startup, so connecting one of the three founding problems meant editing `deploy/.env` and restarting the container. **Every existing rule passed**: CLAUDE.md's CLI-parity constraint and ADR-030 are both conditioned on an endpoint existing, so a capability with zero surfaces owes nothing and is in perfect parity. FPP had already been rescued from this exact pattern in Step 7, and Track D seam D-1 reproduced it afterwards because the rescue was recorded as work done to FPP rather than as a rule.

**The audit**, over 44 API paths, 22 `showmeshctl` commands, 16 UI routes, all 30 coordinator environment variables and the coordinator binary's own subcommands, found four capabilities on no surface at all (Resolume host, the FPP MQTT collector, the asset store settings, identity administration behind `docker exec` into a shell-less image), one the UI could do and the CLI could not (`PUT /config/show.macro/{id}`), and Track E's entire operator surface missing from the UI. Plus `principal:write`, declared and bundled into the admin role since Step 6 and checked by no handler, the fourth capability this project has shipped that nothing could reach.

**Completed.** [ADR-039](../decisions/ADR-039-operator-configuration-is-store-backed.md), accepted by the owner, and seven seams built in parallel worktrees and opened as PRs #6 through #12. [TRACK-G-surface-parity.md](TRACK-G-surface-parity.md) carries the seam table and what each closes. [IDENTIFIER-REGISTER.md](IDENTIFIER-REGISTER.md) is new: the authoritative register for every scarce identifier except ADR numbers, which is why there was no such register when two branches minted ADR-034 twice and exit codes 11 and 12 collided.

**Decisions made:** ADR-039 (owner). Class 3 scoped out and back in the same day as seam G-8 (owner). Two queued for the owner in `docs/private/DECISION-QUEUE.md`: G-3's broker credential stored in a 0600 file rather than in the payload, which honours decision 7's load-bearing half and diverges from its literal text; and `SHOWMESH_INTEGRATION_BROKERS`, a fifth stranded capability.

**A specification error, caught by a builder.** Track G's G-5 section listed `invalidate-all-sessions` as an API capability. That contradicts ADR-024 decision 9, which puts lockout recovery on a host-level subcommand not reachable over the API at any scope. An API path for it would undo every session revocation, reachable exactly when the API's own authority is in doubt. The builder refused to build it and said why; the spec was corrected rather than the code.

**Verification gates.** `make check`, `go test -race ./...` and `make test-integration` green per seam and on the folded tree (645 UI tests, 435s race run on `internal/coordinator/api`). Both G-7 guards were deliberately broken and confirmed to fail naming the right thing, then reverted, verified independently by the orchestrator rather than taken on report. Cold-start acceptance runs per seam proved zero-to-one-and-back-to-zero with no restart.

**Not proved.** Nothing ran against real show hardware. G-2 used a stub rather than a real Arena. G-8's write-scope flows were never exercised authenticated in a browser, and that seam added roughly 2,450 lines of UI with no test files of its own. Both are on `docs/private/PUNCH-LIST.md`. **No Track G PR has merged to `main`.**

**Deferred:** `SHOWMESH_INTEGRATION_BROKERS`; `GET /audit` cannot be paged past 500 entries because its wire type carries no cursor; the `Access.tsx` and Track E view unit tests.
